de-payroll.before: **Minijob rules.** The limit is on regular monthly pay; an unforeseeable overrun in not more than two calendar months within the twelve months ending with the pay period, each by up to the limit itself, does not end the Minijob ([§ 8(1b) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__8.html)). Several Minijobs are added together; one Minijob beside a main insured job stays separate, every further one is added to the main job ([§ 8(2) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__8.html)). A Minijobber is in pension insurance unless they apply in writing or electronically to be released ([§ 6(1b) SGB VI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_6/__6.html)); the employer's 15% stays. The flat tax is an option: the employer may tax by the ELStAM instead. The 2% flat tax is collected by the Minijob-Zentrale (Deutsche Rentenversicherung Knappschaft-Bahn-See, [§ 40a(6) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__40a.html)); 20% and 25% go on the wage tax return. Exactly EUR 603 is a Minijob ("nicht übersteigt"); EUR 603.01 is in the transition band. If aggregation shows that the minor-employment conditions fail, insurance begins on the day the competent insurance decision is notified under § 8(2) SGB IV, unless the employer intentionally or grossly negligently failed to investigate the facts needed to assess insurance status. This is the specific aggregation rule, not a universal bar on retroactive insurance.
de-payroll.after:
**Minijob rules.** The limit is on regular monthly pay; an unforeseeable overrun in not more than two calendar months within the twelve months ending with the pay period, each by up to the limit itself, does not end the Minijob ([§ 8(1b) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__8.html)). Several Minijobs are added together; one Minijob beside a main insured job stays separate, every further one is added to the main job ([§ 8(2) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__8.html)). A Minijobber is in pension insurance unless they apply in writing or electronically to be released ([§ 6(1b) SGB VI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_6/__6.html)); the employer's 15% stays. The flat tax is an option: the employer may tax by the ELStAM instead. The 2% flat tax is collected by the Minijob-Zentrale (Deutsche Rentenversicherung Knappschaft-Bahn-See, [§ 40a(6) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__40a.html)); 20% and 25% go on the wage tax return. Exactly EUR 603 is a Minijob ("nicht übersteigt"); EUR 603.01 is in the transition band. If aggregation shows that the minor-employment conditions fail, insurance begins on the day the competent insurance decision is notified under § 8(2) SGB IV, unless the employer intentionally or grossly negligently failed to investigate the facts needed to assess insurance status. This is the specific aggregation rule, not a universal bar on retroactive insurance.

**Minimum pension base for a small insured Minijob.** For an isolated full-month pension-insured commercial Minijob, with no other insured employment, exemption or part-month/aggregation interaction, § 163(8) SGB VI uses at least EUR 175. Apply the full 18.6% to max(actual monthly pay, EUR 175), then subtract the employer's rounded 15% share of actual pay to obtain the employee remainder (§ 168(1) no. 1b SGB VI; § 2(1) BVV). At actual pay EUR 100, total pension is EUR 32.55, employer EUR 15.00 and employee EUR 17.55, rather than EUR 3.60. Other-job, exemption and part-month cases require their actual assessment facts; do not apply a universal separate EUR 175 floor to every job.

de-payroll.before: **Tax classes** ([§ 38b EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__38b.html)): I single, or married not meeting III or IV, or with limited tax liability; II as I with the single parent relief; III married, both resident, not permanently separated, with the spouse in V on joint application, and the widowed in the year after the death; IV the default for married couples; V the spouse of a class III employee; VI second and further jobs. Missing wage tax data through the employee's fault: class VI; a technical fault: the expected class for at most three months ([§ 39c(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__39c.html)).
de-payroll.after: **Tax classes** ([§ 38b EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__38b.html)): I for the statutory unlimited-tax-liability single/otherwise ineligible married, widowed or divorced categories, or limited tax liability; II for the unlimited-tax-liability I category with single parent relief; III for married spouses who both meet the statutory unlimited-tax-liability category, are not permanently separated and jointly elect III/V; or the year after death where both spouses met that category and were not permanently separated at death; IV for married spouses meeting that same unlimited category and not permanently separated, absent the III/V election; V for the qualifying IV-category spouse jointly electing III/V; VI for second and further concurrent jobs. For III/IV, the actual § 38b(1) sentence 3 category is § 1(1), § 1(2) or § 1a eligibility, not residence alone; no § 1a entitlement is assumed. Missing wage tax data through the employee's fault: class VI; a technical failure or missing identification number without employee fault: expected actual wage-tax data for at most three calendar months ([§ 39c(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__39c.html)). If identification number/date of birth is still missing after those three months, apply the statutory class VI rule retrospectively. When actual ELStAM arrive in the temporary-data cases, review and correct the prior months as necessary and settle under- or over-withholding at the next payroll (§ 39c(1) sentences 3–5).

de-payroll.before: **Sick pay and the maternity top-up.** Continued pay for up to six weeks per incapacity due to sickness without employee fault, once the job has lasted four weeks without a break; the same illness again gives a new six weeks only after six months free of it, or twelve months after the first incapacity from it began ([§ 3 EntgFG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__3.html)), at the pay for regular working time ([§ 4 EntgFG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__4.html)). During the protection periods and the day of birth the employer pays the difference between EUR 13 and the average net pay per calendar day ([§ 20(1) MuSchG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/muschg_2018/__20.html)); U2 refunds it ([§ 1(2) AAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufag/__1.html)). Under § 4(1a) EntgFG, additional overtime pay is excluded, as are expense reimbursements contingent on actual expenses that do not arise during incapacity. For performance-related remuneration, use the average earnings achievable during the employee's applicable regular working time.
de-payroll.after: **Sick pay and the maternity top-up.** Continued pay for up to six weeks per incapacity due to sickness without employee fault, once the job has lasted four weeks without a break; the same illness again gives a new six weeks only after six months free of it, or twelve months after the first incapacity from it began ([§ 3 EntgFG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__3.html)), at the pay for regular working time ([§ 4 EntgFG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__4.html)). During the protection periods and the day of birth the employer pays the difference between EUR 13 and the average net pay per calendar day from the last three settled calendar months before the protection period ([§ 20(1) MuSchG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/muschg_2018/__20.html)); U2 refunds it ([§ 1(2) AAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufag/__1.html)). Under § 4(1a) EntgFG, additional overtime pay is excluded, as are expense reimbursements contingent on actual expenses that do not arise during incapacity. For performance-related remuneration, use the average earnings achievable during the employee's applicable regular working time. For the ordinary multiple-employer case, add the relevant employers' average daily net wages, subtract EUR 13 once, then allocate that top-up in proportion to each employer's average daily net wage. At independently established daily net EUR 60 and EUR 40, combined EUR 100 less EUR 13 gives EUR 87; employer shares are EUR 52.20 and EUR 34.80, not two separate EUR 13 deductions. The ordinary worksheet assumes ongoing employment and established § 20 net inputs. New employment begun during protection is covered from its start under § 20(1); the specific authorised-dismissal/insolvency cases shift payment to the statutory paying agency under § 20(3). For treaty non-residents whose residence state has the taxing right, § 20(4) uses only social-insurance deductions unless that state does not tax the top-up, in which case all statutory deductions count. This is not a full § 21 proof of each real net-pay input.

germany-payroll.after: 4. **Wage tax data.** Take the tax ID, date of birth, and whether this is the first or a further job; retrieve the ELStAM, enter them in the payroll account, and call up changes "monatlich" ([§ 39e(5) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__39e.html)). Missing data by the employee's fault: class VI. A technical fault or a reason the employee is not responsible for: the expected class for at most three calendar months ([§ 39c(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__39c.html)). If identification number/date of birth remains missing after the three calendar months, apply class VI retrospectively under § 39c(1) sentence 3. Once actual ELStAM arrive for the temporary-data cases, review/correct prior months as necessary and settle under- or over-withholding at the next payroll (§ 39c(1) sentences 4–5).

germany-payroll.before: - **Maternity top-up.** For the protection periods before and after the birth and the day of birth, the employer pays the difference between EUR 13 and the average net pay per calendar day of the last three settled months before the protection period ([§ 20(1) MuSchG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/muschg_2018/__20.html)). With several employers, each pays its share. U2 refunds it in full ([§ 1(2) AAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufag/__1.html)).
germany-payroll.after: - **Maternity top-up.** For the protection periods before and after the birth and the day of birth, the employer pays the difference between EUR 13 and the average net pay per calendar day of the last three settled calendar months before the protection period ([§ 20(1) MuSchG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/muschg_2018/__20.html)).  U2 refunds it in full ([§ 1(2) AAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufag/__1.html)). For the ordinary multiple-employer case, add the relevant employers' average daily net wages, subtract EUR 13 once, then allocate that top-up in proportion to each employer's average daily net wage. At independently established daily net EUR 60 and EUR 40, combined EUR 100 less EUR 13 gives EUR 87; employer shares are EUR 52.20 and EUR 34.80, not two separate EUR 13 deductions. The ordinary worksheet assumes ongoing employment and established § 20 net inputs. New employment begun during protection is covered from its start under § 20(1); the specific authorised-dismissal/insolvency cases shift payment to the statutory paying agency under § 20(3). For treaty non-residents whose residence state has the taxing right, § 20(4) uses only social-insurance deductions unless that state does not tax the top-up, in which case all statutory deductions count. This is not a full § 21 proof of each real net-pay input.
